title: Chapter 45
text: 56 And there was the matter of Dick Turpin. It looked like the same car, except that forever afterwards it seemed able to do 250 miles on a gallon of petrol, ran so quietly that you practically had to put your mouth over the exhaust pipe to see if the engine was firing, and issued its voice-synthesized warnings in a series of exquisite and perfectly phrased haikus, each one original and apt … Late frost burns the bloom Would a fool not let the belt Restrain the body? . . . it would say. And, The cherry blossom Tumbles from the highest tree. One needs more petrol.
